src: 15 · Measure words: 个, 本, 杯
Count things and point at them the Chinese way: number or this / that + measure word + noun.
three books
two cups of tea
This book is good.
How much is this ticket?
a cat
That piece of clothing is expensive.
Which one do you like?
In 三本书 (three books), where does the measure word 本 go?
Between the number and the noun
After the noun
Before the number
Only in questions
Number + measure word + noun.
Which measure word is for flat things like tickets and paper?
张 is for flat things: 一张票.
In a shop, you point and say 这个. What does it mean?
What is it?
this one
how many
that one is cheap
这个 alone means "this one".
Which is the pinyin of 杯 (cup)?
杯 has the first tone: high and level.
'three books' =
Books take 本, between the number and the noun.
'this ticket' =
这 needs a measure word too, and tickets take 张.
Which measure word goes with 衣服 (clothes)?
Tops, coats and most clothes take 件.
'a pair of shoes' =
A pair takes 双: 一双鞋.
three books
Books take the measure word 本: 三本书.
this cup of tea
这 + measure word + noun: 这杯茶.
That cat is very small
那 + measure word + noun: 那只猫, with 只 for animals.
I have three books.
Books take 本.
two cups of coffee
A cup of a drink takes 杯.
How much is this ticket?
Tickets are flat, so they take 张.
two cups of tea
茶 (tea)
Tea in a cup takes the measure word 杯, and two before a measure word is 两.
this book
这 + measure word + noun: 这本书.
I don't have that book.
那 + measure word + noun, and 有 takes 没: 我没有那本书.
16 · Ordering food and drinks
Call the server, order dishes and drinks with the right measure words, ask for no spice, and pay.
Excuse me! (calling the server)
I'd like a bowl of noodles.
Two milk teas, please.
Could I have a glass of water, please?
Not spicy, please.
This is delicious!
Check, please!
What is the safest way to call a server?
服务员 is neutral and normal; 小姐 can sound insulting in the mainland.
"I'd like two milk teas." Which is right?
Two before a measure word is 两, and a cup of a drink takes 杯.
What does 打包 mean in a restaurant?
Pack it to take away.
The check, please.
Not spicy.
One more, please.
打包 is for leftovers or food to go.
Which is the pinyin of 汤 (soup)?
汤 has the first tone; táng with the second tone is 糖, sugar.
How do you call the server?
Call the server 服务员; 小姐 is best avoided in the mainland.
'two milk teas' =
Number + one measure word + noun, and two is 两.
'Not spicy, please.' =
要 takes 不: 不要辣的, "not the spicy kind".
You loved the dumplings. Say:
好吃 is good to eat; 好喝 is only for drinks.
I'd like a bowl of noodles
A bowl takes the measure word 碗, before the noun: 一碗面条.
Two milk teas, please (start with 来)
Two before a measure word is 两: 两杯奶茶.
Check, please! (to the server)
Call 服务员 first, then say 买单; 老师 is for a teacher.
I'd like a bowl of noodles.
A bowl of something takes 碗.
Could I have a glass of water, please?
A glass of a drink takes 杯.
Not spicy, please.
辣 is spicy: 不要辣的, not the spicy kind.
I'd like a cup of coffee.
A cup of coffee takes the measure word 杯: 一杯咖啡.
two bowls of noodles
Two before a measure word is 两, and noodles in a bowl take 碗.
Not spicy, please.
要 (want) is negated with 不, not 没: 不要辣的.
17 · Family and age
Name your family members, say how many people are in your family, and ask someone's age the right way.
My dad is a doctor.
She's my older sister.
I have an older brother.
I have two younger sisters.
How many people are in your family?
There are four people in my family.
How old are you? (to a child)
How old are you? (to an adult)
I'm twenty-five this year.
Which word means "younger brother"?
Older brother is 哥哥; younger brother is 弟弟.
In 我家有四口人, what does 口 do?
It means "and".
It turns the sentence into a question.
It is the measure word for family members.
It means mouth, so the sentence is about food.
口 counts the people in a family: 四口人.
A colleague is about your age. How do you ask "How old are you?"
In the mainland, ask an adult 你多大？; 你几岁？ is mostly for children.
Which is the pinyin of 妈妈 (mom)?
The first 妈 has the first tone, and the second has the neutral tone: māma.
'older brother' =
哥哥 is older, 弟弟 younger.
'I have two older sisters' =
Two people: 两 + 个 + noun.
Asking a six-year-old "How old are you?":
几 expects a small number; no 是 and no 吗.
'There are five people in my family' =
Number + 口 + 人, and no 们 after a number.
I have an older brother
A number needs a measure word before the noun: 一个哥哥.
I have two younger sisters
Two before a measure word is 两: 两个妹妹.
How many people are in your family? (to a friend)
The question word 几 already asks, so no 吗.
There are four people in my family.
Family members are counted with 口 (个 is also heard).
I have two younger brothers.
Younger brother is 弟弟.
I'm 25 this year.
Age is the number + 岁.
I have two older brothers.
Two before a measure word is 两: 两个哥哥.
There are three people in my family.
口 is the measure word for family members: 三口人.
My dad isn't a teacher.
是 is negated with 不, never 没, and 爸爸 needs no 的.
18 · Time and dates
Tell the time, name the days of the week and dates, and put time words where Chinese wants them.
What time is it now?
It's half past three.
ten past two
Today is Monday.
December 3
What's the date today?
I'm going to Beijing tomorrow.
I don't work on Saturdays.
What time do you start work?
How do you say "December 3"?
Big to small: the month first, then the day.
"I'm going to Beijing tomorrow." Where does 明天 go?
At the end, after 北京
Right after 去
Before 去, or at the very start
Anywhere at all
Time words go before the verb, or first in the sentence.
What is 三点半?
half past three
three and a half days
a quarter to three
点 is o'clock and 半 is half.
Which is the pinyin of 号 (day of the month)?
号 has the fourth tone; hǎo with the third tone is 好, good.
'two o'clock' =
Two o'clock is 两点, not 二点.
'December 3' =
Month first, then day; 三月十二号 is March 12.
'I'm going tomorrow' =
The time word goes before the verb.
'What time is it now?' =
几 already asks, so no 吗.
I'm going to Beijing tomorrow (start with 我)
Time goes before the verb: 我明天去北京.
December 3
Big to small: the month, then the day.
I don't work on Saturdays (start with 我)
The day and 不 both go before the verb: 我星期六不工作.
What time is it now?
Ask the hour with 几: 几点.
Today is December 3.
The day of the month is the number + 号.
It's half past two.
Two o'clock is 两点, so half past two is 两点半.
I'm going tomorrow.
when comes first
Time goes before the verb: 我明天去.
I don't work on Saturdays.
星期六 (Saturday) · 不 · 工作
The day goes before the verb, and so does 不: 我星期六不工作.
It's two o'clock now.
Two o'clock is 两点, and 现在 goes first.
19 · 在: at, in, and location words
Say where things and people are, use on, in, next to and across from, and say where you do something.
Where's the bank?
I'm at home.
The phone is in the room.
The bank is next to the supermarket.
I'm in Beijing.
I work at a bank.
He eats at home.
How do you say "I work at a bank"?
在 + place goes before the verb.
Why is 上 needed in 书在桌子上 (the book is on the table)?
上 means "is"
上 makes it a question
A table needs a location word to become a place
上 is the measure word for books
Objects need a location word after them: 桌子上, 房间里.
Which of these needs no location word after 在?
北京 (a city)
桌子 (a table)
椅子 (a chair)
书包 (a schoolbag)
Cities and countries are already places: 我在北京.
Which is the pinyin of 在 (to be at)?
在 has the fourth tone: it falls.
'Where's the bank?' =
Thing + 在 + 哪儿, and no 吗 with a question word.
'I work at a bank' =
在 + place comes before the verb.
'The phone is on the table' =
The location word 上 comes after 桌子.
'The bank is next to the supermarket' =
旁边 (next to) comes after the place it is next to.
I work at a bank
Where it happens goes before the verb: 我在银行工作.
The phone is in the room
The location word comes after the noun: 房间里, in the room.
He eats at home
The place with 在 goes before the verb: 他在家吃饭.
Where's the bank?
Where something is: thing + 在 + place.
The phone is on the table.
On the table: 桌子上, with the location word after the noun.
I work at a bank.
在 + place, before the verb.
I work at a bank.
where comes first
Where it happens goes before the verb: 我在银行工作.
We eat at home.
The place with 在 goes before the verb: 我们在家吃饭.
Where's the restroom?
洗手间 (restroom) · 在 · 哪儿
Thing + 在 + 哪儿: the question word sits in the place slot.
20 · Word order: who · when · where · verb
Build longer sentences in the Chinese line-up: who, when, where, how, and the verb last.
I'm eating at home tomorrow.
We're studying at the library this afternoon.
Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing.
I take the subway to work every day.
I go running in the park at ten on Saturday morning.
I live in Beijing, China.
Where does 明天 (tomorrow) go in "I'm going to the bank tomorrow"?
At the end: 我去银行明天
Before the verb: 我明天去银行
Between 去 and 银行
Anywhere; Chinese order is free
Time goes before the verb (or at the very front), never at the end.
Which sentence is in the right order?
Who, then when, then where, then the verb.
How do you say "on Saturday at ten in the morning"?
Big before small: the day, then the part of the day, then the hour.
I'm working at home today =
When and where both go before the verb: 我今天在家工作.
Which is the pinyin of 明天 (tomorrow)?
明 has the second tone and 天 the first tone: míngtiān.
Saturday at ten in the morning =
Big before small: day, then part of the day, then the hour.
I live in Shanghai =
With 住, 在 + place comes right after the verb.
I take the subway to work =
How you travel goes before the verb 去: 坐地铁去上班.
I'm going to Beijing tomorrow (begin with 我)
Time goes before the verb: 我明天去北京.
We study at the library
Where it happens goes before the verb: 在图书馆学习.
I'm eating at home tomorrow (begin with 我)
When comes first, then where, and both go before the verb.
I'm eating at home tomorrow.
在 + place says where it happens: 在家吃饭.
I take the subway to work every day.
坐 (to ride, literally to sit) is how you take the subway: 坐地铁.
I live in Beijing.
住 is followed by 在 + place: 我住在北京.
I work at a bank
where comes first
Where it happens goes before the verb: 我在银行工作.
I'm going to Shanghai tomorrow
Time goes before the verb, never at the end: 我明天去上海.
We have class at two o'clock on Monday
big before small
Big before small, and the time goes before the verb: 星期一两点上课.
21 · 想, 要, 会, 能: want and can
Say what you want, what you'd like, what you know how to do, and ask if you may.
I'd like some coffee.
I want a cup of coffee.
I have to work tomorrow.
I can speak a little Chinese.
I can't drive.
Can you come tomorrow?
May I come in?
Can you speak Chinese?
I'd like to eat at home.
Which word do you use for a skill you learned, like swimming?
会 means know how to: 我会游泳.
How do you ask "May I come in?"
可以 asks for permission.
"I don't want to go" is…
不 goes in front of 想: 不想去.
Which word means "know how to" (a skill you learned)?
会 is for skills you learned: 我会游泳.
May I sit here? =
可以 comes right after 我 and asks for permission.
Which is the pinyin of 想 (would like)?
想 has the third tone: xiǎng.
I'd like to eat at home tonight =
When first, then 想, then where, and the verb last.
I don't want to go =
不 goes in front of 想: 我不想去.
I'd like to drink a cup of tea
Tea in a cup takes the measure word 杯: 一杯茶.
I want to study at the library
Where it happens goes before the verb: 想在图书馆学习.
I can speak a little Chinese
会 is for a skill you learned, like a language; 是 is not "can".
You may come in.
可以 gives permission: 你可以进来.
I can't drive (I never learned).
A skill you never learned takes 不会.
Waiter, I'd like a bowl of noodles.
With a thing and no verb, want is 要 (or 想要).
I'd like two cups of coffee
Coffee in a cup takes the measure word 杯, and two before it is 两.
I'd like to eat at home (use 想)
Where it happens goes before the verb: 想在家吃饭.
I can't swim (I never learned)
say no with 不
A skill takes 会, and its no is 不会, not 没.
22 · 了: done, and changed (not a past tense)
Use 了 to say an action is done or something has changed, and know when to leave it out.
I bought two tickets.
He drank three cups of coffee.
I went to Shanghai yesterday.
It's gotten cold.
I'm hungry now.
We're here!
I used to take the subway a lot.
I was busy yesterday.
Have you eaten?
What does 了 right after a verb show?
That the sentence is a question
That the action is done
The past tense of every verb
That the action is happening now
了 after a verb shows the action is complete; it is not a past tense.
"I was busy yesterday" is…
A state in the past takes no 了; the time word says when.
What does 天气冷了 mean?
It's gotten cold.
It was cold.
It's not cold.
Is it cold?
了 at the end shows a change: now it's cold.
I bought three tickets =
了 goes right after the verb: 买了三张票.
Which is the pinyin of 买 (to buy)?
买 has the third tone; mài (fourth tone) is 卖, to sell.
I was busy yesterday =
A state in the past takes no 了: 我昨天很忙.
I didn't go yesterday =
After 没 there is no 了.
It's gotten hot. =
了 at the end shows a change: 热了.
I didn't go to work yesterday (begin with 我)
Time goes before the verb, and after 没 there is no 了.
I bought three apples
Apples take the measure word 个: 三个苹果.
It's gotten cold
了 at the end shows a change, and 冷 needs no 是.
I bought three apples.
了 right after the verb shows the buying is done.
I didn't go yesterday.
For something that did not happen, use 没, not 不.
I'm hungry (now).
了 at the end shows a change: 我饿了.
I bought two tickets
Tickets take the measure word 张, and two before it is 两.
I didn't go to the bank yesterday
Time goes before the verb, and after 没 there is no 了.
It's gotten cold
a change
了 at the end shows a change, and adjectives take no 是.
23 · 在 and 正在: doing it right now
Say what someone is doing right now, and ask what they are doing.
He's watching TV.
What are you doing?
I'm eating right now.
Mom is on the phone.
He's at home watching TV.
How do you say "I'm eating" (right now)?
在 before the verb shows the action is going on; 是 is not "am".
Which word can go at the end to add "right now"?
呢 at the end goes with 在 or 正在 for an action in progress.
"I'm going to Shanghai tomorrow" (a plan) is…
A plan takes no 在: 在 is for an action happening now.
I'm eating =
在 before the verb means in the middle of; 是 is not "am".
Which is the pinyin of 在?
在 has the fourth tone: it falls, zài.
What are you doing? =
The question word stays where the answer goes: 在做什么.
I'm going to Shanghai tomorrow (a plan) =
A plan takes no 在; 在 is for what is going on now.
He's at home watching TV =
Where it happens goes before the verb, and 呢 goes at the very end.
I'm watching TV at home right now
Where it happens goes before the verb, and 呢 goes at the end.
We're having class right now (use 正在)
正在 goes before the verb: 我们正在上课.
What are you doing?
Chinese has no -ing: 在 + verb, and 是 is not "are".
He's watching TV.
在 or 正在 before the verb shows the action is going on.
I'm eating right now.
呢 at the end goes with 正在 for right now.
Mom is on the phone in the kitchen.
在 + place says where it is happening: 在厨房.
He's watching TV
Chinese has no -ing: 在 or 正在 goes before the verb.
I'm studying at the library
Where it happens goes before the verb: 在图书馆学习.
What are you doing? (to a friend)
什么 stays where the answer goes, after 在 + verb.
24 · Two verbs in a row: 去 + verb
Say where you're going and what you'll do there, and how you get there, with no word for "to".
I'm going to the supermarket to buy some things.
He's coming to my place for dinner.
Tomorrow I'm going to the bank to change money.
I go to school by subway.
She rides her bike to work.
We're flying to Chengdu.
Tomorrow I'm taking the high-speed train to Xi'an to see the Terracotta Warriors.
I'm not going to the bank to change money tomorrow.
How do you say "I'm going to the supermarket to buy things"?
Go to the place first, then what you do there.
Which verb do you use to ride the subway or a bus?
坐 (literally sit) is for anything you ride inside.
Where does "by subway" go in "I go to school by subway"?
Before 去: 我坐地铁去学校
At the end: 我去学校坐地铁
Between 去 and 学校
Before 我
How you travel comes before 去.
I'm going to the bank to change money =
Go to the place first, then what you do there: 去银行换钱.
Which is the pinyin of 去 (to go)?
去 has the fourth tone: qù.
She rides her bike to school =
骑 for a bike, and how you go comes before 去.
Which verb means "ride" for buses, the subway and planes?
坐 (literally sit) is for anything you ride inside; 骑 is for bikes.
He's coming to my place for dinner =
来 + place first, then what he will do: 来我家吃饭.
I'm going to the supermarket to buy things
Where you go comes before the verb of what you do there: 去超市买东西.
I go to school by subway
How you go comes before the verb 去: 坐地铁去学校.
Tomorrow I'm going to Beijing to see the Great Wall (begin with 我)
Time goes before both verbs: 我明天去北京看长城.
I'm going to the supermarket to buy things.
买 (mǎi) is buy; 卖 (mài) is sell.
I ride my bike to work.
You ride a bike astride: 骑自行车.
He's coming to my place for dinner.
来 + place: he comes to my place, then eats.
I'm going to the bank to change money
Where you go comes before the verb of what you do there: 去银行换钱.
I take the subway to work
How you go comes before the verb: 坐地铁去上班.
I'm going to the store to buy two bottles of water
商店 (store) · 买 · 两 · 瓶 · 水
Water in a bottle takes the measure word 瓶, and two before it is 两.
25 · Verb-not-verb questions: 去不去
Ask yes/no questions the second Chinese way, verb + 不 + verb, and answer them.
Are you going?
Are you a teacher?
Is it cold today?
Do you have an older brother?
Do you like tea?
Are you coming tomorrow?
Is this book expensive?
Do you have time?
Which question is correct?
No 很 and no 吗: just 忙不忙.
What is the verb-not-verb question for 有?
有 is negated with 没, so the question is 有没有.
How do you answer 你去不去？ with yes?
Answer with the verb itself: 去 or 不去.
Are you busy? =
No 很 and no 吗: just 忙不忙.
Which is the pinyin of 去不去？
In a verb-not-verb question 不 takes the neutral tone: qù bu qù.
Do you have a car? =
有 is negated with 没, so the question is 有没有.
Do you like coffee? =
A two-character verb: 喜不喜欢 or 喜欢不喜欢, with no 吗.
How do you answer 你去不去？ with yes?
Answer with the verb itself: 去 or 不去.
Are you coming tomorrow? (begin with 你)
Time goes before the verb, even in a question: 你明天来不来？
Is this book expensive?
Books take the measure word 本: 这本书贵不贵？
Do you have an older brother?
有 takes 没, so the question is 有没有, with no 吗.
Are you going?
Verb + 不 + verb makes the question: 去不去.
Do you have a Chinese book?
有 is negated only with 没: 有没有.
Do you like tea?
Say the whole verb again after 不: 喜欢不喜欢.
Are you coming tomorrow? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
Time goes before the verb: 你明天来不来？
Do you want this cup of tea? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
A cup of something takes the measure word 杯: 这杯茶.
Is your older brother a teacher? (to a friend, use verb-not-verb)
是不是 already asks the question, so there is no 吗.
26 · 也, 都, 还: also, all, still
Say "too", "all", "both", "still" and "not yet" with the words in the right place.
I'm American too.
She's busy too.
I don't drink coffee either.
We're all students.
My mom and dad both like tea.
They're all teachers too.
None of us drinks.
I haven't eaten yet.
What else would you like?
He's still sleeping.
Where does 也 go in "I'm a student too"?
At the end: 我是学生也
At the start: 也我是学生
Before the verb: 我也是学生
After the verb: 我是也学生
也 goes after the subject, right before the verb.
What does 我们都不喝酒 mean?
None of us drinks.
Not all of us drink.
We all drink.
We don't drink yet.
都不 means none; 不都 would mean not all.
"I haven't eaten yet" is…
还没 + verb means not yet, with no 了.
I'm a student too =
也 goes after the subject and before the verb.
Which is the pinyin of 也 (also)?
也 has the third tone: yě.
We're all American =
都 comes after 我们 and before the verb.
I haven't eaten yet =
还没 + verb means not yet, with no 了.
None of us is going =
都不 means none; 不都 means not all.
My dad is a teacher too
也 goes before the verb, never at the end like English too.
We all like to drink tea
都 goes after 我们 and before the verb: 我们都喜欢喝茶.
They're all at home
都 goes before the verb 在: 他们都在家.
She's American too.
也 (also) goes before 是: 她也是美国人.
We're all students.
都 (all) looks back at 我们: 我们都是学生.
I haven't eaten yet.
还没 means not yet.
I'm American too
也 goes before the verb, not at the end like English too.
We both have a cat
都 goes before the verb, and cats take the measure word 只.
My mom and dad are both busy
都 goes before the verb or adjective, and adjectives take 很, not 是.
27 · 吧 and 别: let's, and don't
Suggest things with 吧, tell people not to with 别, and ask politely with 请 and 麻烦你.
Let's go.
Why don't you give it a try?
Let's go to the hospital tomorrow.
Don't worry.
Don't go!
No talking.
Come in, please.
Could you speak more slowly, please?
Could you give me a hand?
OK, fine.
How do you say "Let's go"?
吧 at the end of a 我们 sentence means let's.
How do you say "Don't worry"?
别 + verb tells someone not to do something.
Where does 请 go in "Come in, please"?
Before the verb: 请进
After the verb: 进请
At the end with 吧: 进吧请
It is not used here
请 comes first, then the verb: 请进.
Let's go =
吧 at the end of a 我们 sentence means let's.
Which is the pinyin of 请 (please)?
请 has the third tone: qǐng; qíng with the second tone is 晴, sunny.
Don't worry =
别 + verb means don't; 不 only says not.
Come in, please =
请 goes first, then the verb.
Could you give me a hand? =
麻烦你 goes first, then the request.
Let's eat at home (begin with 我们)
Where it happens goes before the verb, and 吧 goes at the end.
Let's go to the hospital tomorrow (begin with 我们)
Time goes before the verb: 我们明天去医院吧.
Please don't worry
请 goes first, then 别 + verb for don't: 请别担心.
